This is terrible reporting right here. We do NOT have any cases of bacteria being resistant to ALL antibiotics. What we have is the first case of a bacteria showing resistance to our antibacterial drug 'of last resort'. Now we have all the pieces to make a superbug floating around in the US, but we have not seen them all put together. The case in question here was still treatable with current antibiotics.

However, the risk of a superbug is out there, and something we do not want to be caught defenseless again. Years of privately led R&D have by and large ignored this, because Antibiotics are not a good profit earner. They have to be made cheaply to be of any great use, and they outright -cure- the problem. Unfortunately, private research is all profit-based, and there's little profit to be had by inventing cheap cures to illness. It's far more profitable to find a drug that manages symptoms without eliminating the disease, and that's where the bulk of research efforts go.

Between the lack of development in needed areas, the outlandish profiteering we've seen becoming commonplace, and shady research practices becoming standard (Run 50 studies but only report the one that comes in favorably for you, etc), it's clear that medical research cannot be left entirely in the hands of the private sector. Someone needs to undertake medical research that's truly for the common good, and I can't think of a way for that to happen that does not involve the government getting involved.
